Reproduced by mutation: a /tmp copy of plugins/playbook/tasks/compact.py whose --dry-run arm appends one unrelated line to task.md before returning still passes the bound proof (byte-identical False, stray line present True, proof OK); the control mutant that instead lets --dry-run perform the real compaction IS caught (proof red).

The no-write and byte-identity clauses are retained because the command asserts them to the user at runtime - it prints the `[dry-run] N block(s) ... would move` preview and performs no write on that arm - so they are a live public promise rather than a claim this ledger invented. Byte identity is inferred from the early `return` in the dry_run arm reached by tasks/compact.py::cmd_compact, not proved.

Exact byte-identity evidence (compare task.md bytes before and after the dry-run, the idiom tests/test_inspection_flags_are_dry.py already uses) is scheduled for Phase 3; adding it is a product-test change and is deliberately NOT performed in Phase 1.
